units.source_text: Each treatment day includes intravenous doxorubicin followed by a 3-hour ifosfamide infusion, with prescribed mesna and fluids. Confirm who manages the mesna pump and when it is disconnected; do not alter pump settings yourself.

units.source_text: Mesna and prescribed hydration are essential bladder protection. units.source_text: Ask / act: Call oncology immediately for fever, shaking chills, suddenly feeling unwell, unusual bleeding, new breathlessness, very little urine, severe rash or vomiting that prevents drinking. Follow your hospital’s temperature and contact instructions. Severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, collapse or seizures: call 112/999. New breathlessness, reduced urine, severe abdominal pain or diarrhoea, widespread blistering rash, rapid swelling or new visual symptoms needs urgent assessment. Fever is never assumed to be only a flu-like drug effect.

units.source_text: Take dexamethasone 8 mg by mouth twice daily for 3 days, starting day 7, unless your team prescribes an explicitly revised plan; NCCP requires at least 3 doses before docetaxel. This reduces allergic reactions and fluid retention. Both drugs have low emetogenic classification in this source. granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (white-cell growth support) (G-CSF) may be used based on the prescribed risk plan; it is not mandatory for every patient in NCCP 00501.
